findings.desc: CHK-004 userSees promises: "reviewer_batch and escalation guidance print launch lines like \"lattice host_run --host codex --storyId B-xxxx --agentType reviewer --reviewRunId ... --lane ...\" instead of raw codex exec commands, and docs/host-run-usage.md exists." The doc file (docs/host-run-usage.md) was delivered accurately, but the reviewer_batch guidance was NOT changed at all (git diff main -- packages/main/src/handlers/reviewer-batch.ts is empty) and still only ever emits the in-process Agent(...) subagent launch form (verified live via `lattice reviewer_batch` in this session, e.g. `Agent({ subagent_type: "lattice-review-docs", prompt: "Review story B-70e9 (touchpoints .md)" })`), never `lattice host_run`. review-escalation.ts DID change, but only to add CHK-003 usage-ledger recording (recordHostReadinessProbeUsage) -- it contains no printed guidance-string changes either. The plan.md CHK-004 premise (line 71/79: rewrite raw codex exec / claude --print / agy --print operator-facing instruction strings in these two files) was already false pre-story: `git show main -- reviewer-batch.ts / review-escalation.ts` shows neither file ever printed a raw host-CLI instruction string to rewrite (reviewer_batch only ever used Agent(...); review-escalation.ts had none). CHK-004 evidence notes even acknowledge this ("OQ-2: no raw-launch instruction strings existed to rewrite"), but the checklist userSees text was never corrected to match, so it stands as a literal unfulfilled user-facing promise.
findings.dismissReason: The userSees sentence encodes a premise that was already false before this story: git show main -- packages/main/src/handlers/reviewer-batch.ts / review-escalation.ts contains no raw codex exec / claude --print / agy --print instruction string to rewrite (reviewer_batch has only ever emitted in-session Agent(...) subagent launches, which are deliberately out of scope per CHK-004 verificationIntent edge case). Scope OQ-2 was resolved in writing at PLAN with behavior-based acceptance: the delivered guidance surface is docs/host-run-usage.md (host_run launch lines with binding args for reviewer/quorum host runs) plus the grep-verified absence of raw-launch instruction strings in handlers. userSees text is frozen from DEV by design, so correcting the wording retroactively is not possible without reopening PLAN; the FINDING is accepted as a wording mismatch, not a functional gap. TEST-phase delivery check will verify the doc-based guidance instead.

findings.desc: All 42 must-priority verificationEvidence rows across CHK-001..CHK-007 are currently STALE per lattice validate / evidence_plan (verificationCoverage covered=0/42, missingRequired=42), so the DONE gate would see ZERO valid coverage right now despite the underlying tests genuinely passing. Root cause: evidence was recorded at DEV commit b8d52bbdb (materialHash=9a34267cfc.../storyFilesHash=9df50ebfa3...), then main was merged into story/B-70e9 at 7031fa81c (bringing in an unrelated story B-b264 DONE + a version bump touching package.json/packages/main/package.json), which shifted both materialHash (now 1f57a4081...) and storyFilesHash (now 31513ec6c...) even though none of B-70e9's own story files changed content. Independently confirmed: npm --prefix packages/main run test:host-run-usage (25/25 pass) and test:usage-sweep (11/11 pass) both pass cleanly against current HEAD 867de85e6, and evidence_plan classifies all 42 as refresh-only (hash drift, not rerun_required/hard_stale/missing) -- so this is a re-stamp issue, not a real coverage gap. Needs verification_evidence_refresh_stale / evidence_refresh --apply (or fresh verification_evidence_add) before TEST/DONE so the gate sees the coverage that genuinely exists.
findings.resolvedReason: Ran lattice verification_evidence_refresh_stale for B-70e9 after the deliberate main merge (B-b264 landed on main mid-story; only unrelated version-bump files shifted the whole-tree materialHash/storyFilesHash). evidence_plan now reports missing=0 rerun=0 refresh-only=0 fresh=42. The underlying smokes were independently re-run by the test-coverage reviewer at the post-merge tree (test:host-run-usage 25/25, test:usage-sweep 11/11), so the re-stamp binds passing evidence to the current hashes rather than papering over a real gap.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r1] Concurrency cap is check-then-acquire and can be bypassed by concurrent starts: the cap decision scans live slots BEFORE this process creates its own uniquely-named slot file (host-run.ts ~line 570 scan, ~line 605 unconditional acquire of <pid>-<monotonic>.json). Two or more host_run processes starting simultaneously can all observe live < cap, all acquire distinct slots, and all spawn - the documented fail-closed concurrency cap is not enforced under the exact concurrent workload it exists to control. The smoke atomic-race check only exercised wx collision on the SAME filename, which never happens with unique names. Fix direction (codex): fixed numbered slot files slot-0..slot-(cap-1) with exclusive create so only cap contenders can succeed; stale reclaim per slot by pid/mtime.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 8a8cd2407: replaced check-then-acquire with atomic fixed-numbered slot admission (slot-0..slot-(cap-1), exclusive wx create IS the admission decision; stale reclaim re-probes immediately before unlink and treats lost EEXIST races as moves to the next index, never guaranteed admission). Smoke replaced the fake same-filename race with real contention checks that provably fail against the old primitive: cap=1 second admission without release must return null (old unique-name acquire always succeeded), plus a stale-reclaim race with exactly-one-winner assertion. host-run-usage smoke 27/27; full usage-ledger group green.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r1] Blocked codex/agy host runs are recorded as Anthropic usage rows: host_run calls the budget and concurrency block recorders for all three hosts, but those paths use finalContext(), which hard-codes provider.name=anthropic (dispatch-usage.ts ~line 776). A codex or agy hard-budget/concurrency refusal writes its blocked ledger row under the wrong provider, breaking the provider-bound attribution this story claims and corrupting usage diagnostics. Stage A implementer had flagged this as deviation 3 (kept byte-compatible with buildBlockedBudgetRecord); codex confirms it is a real defect. Fix direction: thread the actual host provider into the blocked-record path (provider-parametric contexts for openai/anthropic/antigravity) and add smoke assertions that codex and agy refusals persist provider.name as openai and antigravity respectively.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 8a8cd2407: buildBlockedBudgetRecord gained a trailing providerName param (default anthropic keeps every legacy caller byte-identical); recordBudgetBlock/recordConcurrencyBlock accept optional provider {name,model}; host_run threads codex->openai / claude->anthropic / agy->antigravity into BOTH blocked paths. Smoke asserts codex budget-block rows carry provider.name=openai, agy concurrency-block rows carry antigravity, and claude blocked rows keep the legacy anthropic shape field-by-field. Would fail against old code which hard-coded anthropic at the builder.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r2c] Story-bound host_run ignores configured storyDir: resolvePhase hard-codes .lattice/story/actives (host-run.ts ~line 177) before honoring even an explicit --phase. Projects configuring storyDir in lattice.config.json use the store/config for story metadata everywhere else in the CLI; in such projects every story-bound host_run is refused as unknown story and no host launches. Fix direction: resolve the story via the handler ctx.store (or loadConfig storyDir) and only fail unknown-story against the configured path; when --phase is supplied do not require the index read at all.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 4f5e980f1: removed the hard-coded .lattice/story/actives read from core; phase resolution goes through an injected HostRunStoryResolver built from ctx.store.readStory in the handler (honors configured storyDir); explicit --phase never consults the store (resolver call count 0 asserted); unknown story via configured store still refuses pre-spawn when no phase is given. New smokes prove the exact old failure modes.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r2c] host_run buffers instead of streaming host stdout: the default runner uses spawnSync with piped stdio, withholding all host output until exit, despite the documented contract (docs/host-run-usage.md + CHK-001 DoneWhen: host stdout passes through live, line-streamed, memory-bounded). Long reviewer/quorum runs lose progress observability (the exact B-d8ef complaint) and outputs beyond the 64MiB maxBuffer fail/truncate rather than stream. Fix direction: production runner switches to async spawn, chunks pass through to the caller as they arrive (text mode; json mode routes passthrough to stderr or suppresses it, documented), retaining only bounded data for usage parsing; injected runner seam stays for tests.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 4f5e980f1: default runner switched to async child_process.spawn with live chunk passthrough (text mode stdout->stdout, json mode->stderr keeping stdout clean), UsageLineScanner retains only the last usage-bearing line capped at 1MiB with honest retentionTruncated -> unavailable on parse miss, no 64MiB maxBuffer, exactly-once delivery (no double print), SIGKILL/timeout semantics preserved. Streaming smoke asserts first line reaches the sink >=80ms before exit; smoke total now 33.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: F-006 spawnSync-to-async-spawn replacement left a stale forward-looking doc comment: packages/main/src/handlers/host-run.ts:61 CreateHostRunHandlersOptions.runner JSDoc still says 'production uses the piped spawnSync default', but production now uses the async child_process.spawn streaming defaultHostRunRunner (core/host-run.ts). This is not a historical/comparative reference (unlike the two correct comments at core/host-run.ts:715 and tasks/host-run-usage-smoke.ts:566 which explicitly say 'previous'/'old spawnSync') — it is stated as current fact and will mislead future readers of this file changed in this very commit.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit b8908661f: handlers/host-run.ts:61 JSDoc updated to describe the async streaming defaultHostRunRunner (child_process.spawn, live chunk passthrough, bounded usage-line retention); no spawnSync claim remains.

findings.desc: core/host-run.ts:770-777 defaultHostRunRunner: onChunk (and therefore the handler's passthrough, which does raw process.stdout.write/process.stderr.write) is invoked synchronously inside the child.stdout/stderr 'data' listeners with no try/catch. If the passthrough sink throws (e.g. EPIPE when a downstream consumer of host_run output closes early, a common real-world case for `lattice host_run | head` or a killed reviewer pipe), the exception is uncaught inside a Node EventEmitter callback and crashes the whole process: the spawned child is orphaned (no SIGKILL, since finish() in the same runner never runs), runHostRun's `finally { releaseSlot(slotFile) }` (host-run.ts:1008-1010) never executes so the concurrency slot leaks until the staleness backstop reclaims it hours later, and no ledger final row is written. No global uncaughtException/EPIPE handler exists anywhere in packages/main/src to catch this. Fix direction: wrap the onChunk call (or the passthrough sink itself, in both defaultHostRunRunner and the handler's passthrough) in try/catch so a downstream write failure degrades gracefully instead of crashing the host run and leaking the slot.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit b8908661f: all passthrough deliveries route through first-failure-guarded safeDeliver/deliver wrappers; first onChunk throw flips passthroughBroken (no per-chunk retry), chunks keep feeding the UsageLineScanner, the run completes with honest passthroughError surfaced in result/JSON and a text-mode stderr warning; ledger final row and slot release proven intact. Verified failing-before (old build crashes with uncaught EventEmitter exception / runHostRun rejects) and passing-after via standalone repro plus new smoke check; host-run-usage smoke 34/34.

findings.desc: handlers/host-run.ts:61 CreateHostRunHandlersOptions.runner JSDoc comment is stale spawnSync residue: "Test seam: inject a fake host runner (production uses the piped spawnSync default)." This describes the PRE-F-006 implementation. Since commit 4f5e980f1, the production default is defaultHostRunRunner (core/host-run.ts:718), an ASYNC child_process.spawn with live streaming passthrough -- not a piped spawnSync. The comment misleads a future reader about the actual production runner and directly contradicts the file header comment at handlers/host-run.ts:1-31 (which correctly documents the live-streaming behavior) and core/host-run.ts:710-716. Fix: update the comment to reference the async streaming defaultHostRunRunner.
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of F-007 (same stale JSDoc line at handlers/host-run.ts:61), fixed by the same commit b8908661f.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r3] usage_sweep --out can clobber arbitrary project files despite the read-only classification: handlers/usage-sweep.ts ~line 173 writes the report with writeFileSync directly to the caller-selected --out path after only a lexical inside-root check. A non-owner session can pass --out package.json (or any tracked file) and truncate/replace it, and the guard does not reject symlink ancestors so an inside-root symlink can redirect the write outside the project. Violates the command read-only/no-mutation contract. Fix direction (codex): hardened output helper - require a relative report path, reject existing files, lstat/realpath every existing ancestor rejecting symlink traversal or outside-root resolution, write with exclusive create flag.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit e3ac9b651: replaced the lexical resolveOutPathWithinRoot with hardened openReportFileExclusive in core/usage-sweep.ts - relative-only paths, per-ancestor lstat rejecting symlinks, realpath containment against realpathed root, mkdir only after validation, and O_EXCL exclusive create so overwrite is impossible atomically (already-exists is a typed refusal). Handler writes via the returned fd only; docs updated to create-only semantics. 5 new handler-level smoke checks each provably fail against the old code (absolute-in-root allowed, w-flag truncation of package.json, symlink escape write, silent second-run overwrite); usage-sweep smoke 16/16, host-run 34/34.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r4] host_run launches hosts from the caller cwd instead of the resolved project root: runHostRun builds HostRunSpawnPlan without cwd (core/host-run.ts ~line 907) although defaultHostRunRunner honors plan.cwd; the CLI engine resolves --root into ctx.root but does not chdir, so lattice --root <worktree> host_run invoked from elsewhere spawns codex/claude/agy in the wrong working directory while ledger attribution still points at the requested story/root - an independent reviewer can inspect the wrong repository. Fix direction: thread explicit cwd through HostRunArgs/HostRunSpawnPlan, set to the resolved project/worktree root in the handler, pass into the runner plan, smoke test with process.cwd != ctx.root.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit e27341a4ff: HostRunArgs gains required cwd threaded into HostRunSpawnPlan for every spawn path with a pre-spawn fail-closed guard (missing cwd refuses before any ledger row); handler binds cwd: ctx.root - literally the same value used as ledger root/projectRootHash so execution and attribution cannot diverge (deliberately NOT resolveStoryCommandWorkspace, which throws for adhoc runs and itself consults process.cwd). Two new smoke checks: fake-runner plan.cwd equals injected root while process.cwd differs, and a real child printing process.cwd bound to the injected root. host-run smoke 36/36.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r5] Concurrent host_run ledger writes can corrupt the hash chain: host_run writes the preflight row BEFORE slot admission so simultaneous starts all reach appendUsageRecord, and appendUsageRecord computes previousRecordHash by reading the current last line then appending with no cross-process lock - two processes can read the same predecessor and append rows whose previousRecordHash makes verifyLedgerChain fail. Ledger is default-ON and host_run explicitly supports concurrency (cap 4), so the race is in the feature expected path. Fix direction: serialize appends with a cross-process lock around read-last-hash..append at the single-writer choke point (writer), plus a parallel-writes smoke asserting verifyLedgerChain passes after concurrent preflight/final/block writes.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit bc966e3247: appendUsageRecord wraps the read-last-hash->append critical section in an atomic mkdir cross-process lock (sibling llm-usage.jsonl.lock/), bounded wait 5s (LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER_LOCK_WAIT_MS) with 25ms retries via Atomics.wait, stale reclaim at 30s mtime (LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_MS); on timeout the writer throws through its existing failure contract so the seam fail-open yields an honest under-count instead of a corrupt chain (skip-not-corrupt comment in code). Failing-before demonstrated: same 6x5 parallel harness against the old writer produced CHAIN BROKEN at line 3; fixed writer passes verifyLedgerChain 30/30 across 3 consecutive runs. Three new smoke checks (parallel chain, stale reclaim, bounded-wait skip); host-run smoke 39/39; all 9 usage-ledger smokes green.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r6] Truncated final usage line can record stale provider usage: UsageLineScanner keeps the previously retained usage line when a later over-cap line is dropped and sets retentionTruncated, but runHostRun (~line 1094) ignores spawn.retentionTruncated and passes only spawn.stdout to recordFinalForHost. If a codex/claude run emits a valid usage event and then the REAL final usage-bearing line exceeds the 1MiB cap, the ledger records the stale earlier provider-reported usage instead of unavailable - violating the no-fabricated/no-stale-value contract and mis-counting the run. Fix direction: thread spawn.retentionTruncated into recordFinalForHost and when true record a provider-specific unavailable final (reason retention_truncated) without parsing retained stdout; regression: valid usage line followed by over-cap final usage line.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit a967792ab4: runHostRun threads spawn.retentionTruncated into recordFinalForHost; when true, codex/claude record a provider-specific unavailable final (reason usage_line_retention_truncated) WITHOUT parsing the retained stdout, and the usage summary reports unavailable with that reason (agy keeps its more specific reason). Two regression checks drive the REAL runner+scanner path: valid usage line followed by an over-cap final line asserts precondition (stale line retained), then unavailable final + zero provider-reported rows + no stale numbers in the summary. Failing-before proven by reverting the call site flag in the compiled output (both checks fail recording the stale final); host-run smoke 41/41.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r7] usage_sweep --out bypasses read-only gates: the command is ownershipClass=readOnly / destructiveRisk=none (command-policy.ts ~471) but the handler creates a report file when --out is supplied; reviewer-readonly and retired-root gates allow effective readOnly commands, so a read-only reviewer session can still create arbitrary new files inside the project root and change the material tree. Fix direction: make usage_sweep dynamically mutating when args.out is non-empty (mirror the existing --write boundary rules in resolveEffectiveOwnershipClass) and update policy/process-fact/destructive-risk text, or reject --out under reviewer read-only/retired-root modes.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 2951090b79: resolveEffectiveOwnershipClass (cli/ownership-gate.ts) gains the usage_sweep rule mirroring the --write precedents - non-empty args.out resolves to storyScopedMutating (blocked by reviewer-readonly and retired-root gates), absent/blank --out stays readOnly; policy/process-fact text updated honestly; smoke check 17 asserts both branches as a pure resolver call. Failing-before: the resolver returned readOnly with out set, so reviewer gates allowed file creation.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r7] Host readiness ledger records phantom LLM calls: recordHostReadinessProbeUsage (handlers/review-escalation.ts ~191) writes preflight+unavailable finals for EVERY probed host, but the availability probe returns rows for hosts that never spawned the readiness prompt at all (missing executable, failed --version). Those non-calls become ledger records and inflate unknown attempt counts, contradicting host-side LLM usage capture. Fix direction: filter on whether an execution attempt actually happened (probe result failureKind not in {missing_executable, version_failed} / executablePath+versionOk present) before recording rows; skip ledger writes for hosts where no LLM subprocess launched.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 2951090b79: recordHostReadinessProbeUsage filters through readinessProbeSubprocessLaunched - skips missing_executable, version_failed, and pre-spawn wrong_launcher (no exitCode/outputBytes evidence), keeps timeout/auth/silent_final_output/none which imply a real spawn; call site threads failureKind/exitCode/outputBytes from the frozen probe rows. Smoke constructs all four cases from real classifyHostExecutionReadiness rows and proves rows exist only for the attempted host. Failing-before: every probed host produced 2 phantom rows.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r8] Autopilot repair launches bypass the new pre-spawn caps: runClaudeRepair (core/autopilot-executor.ts ~314) records a usage preflight when the ledger is enabled but then invokes the Claude runner directly - it never applies recordBudgetBlock or the host-run concurrency slot guard, so LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS or a saturated LATTICE_HOST_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT will not stop an autopilot repair even though the story adds those caps for every lattice-initiated host run. Fix direction: factor the same budget and concurrency admission (blocked ledger rows included) into the repair path before calling the runner, reusing the exported host-run primitives; ledger OFF stays byte-identical.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 3f3dea9bcd: runClaudeRepair ledger-ON path now runs the same admission chain as runHostRun in the same order (preflight -> recordBudgetBlock -> acquireHostRunSlot -> spawn -> releaseSlot in finally), returning an honest failed attempt (exitCode 3, reason in stderrExcerpt) without spawning on refusal; slot-registry errors fail closed without faking cap rows. Ledger OFF byte-identical (env-pinned in smoke). host-run smoke 44/44 with failing-before proven by reverting the file; budget-smoke import fence gained autopilot-executor as the third authorized recordBudgetBlock site.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r9] Cross-host Codex review bypasses the hard-budget guard: the usage-ledger binding in codex-review-leaf (~line 524) records a preflight estimate then immediately invokes the runner without recordBudgetBlock or slot admission, so cross_host_review launches an expensive codex subprocess even when LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS would block the same prompt through host_run/autopilot repair. Fix direction: after recordDispatchPreflight run the same budget admission with provider openai; if blocked, record the blocked row and return a synthesized blocked verdict without calling the runner; apply the host-run concurrency slot as well so the cap covers all lattice-initiated host spawns.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit b5df58d44d: codex-review-leaf ledger-ON path now runs the same admission chain as host_run/autopilot-repair (preflight -> recordBudgetBlock provider openai -> acquireHostRunSlot -> spawn -> releaseSlot in finally); refusal synthesizes a decision=blocked verdict (reason budget_blocked/concurrency_cap_exceeded, exitCode 3, no spawn, no fabricated pass/fail) which cross_host_review surfaces as hostB=blocked / joint=blocked; slot-registry errors fail closed without fake cap rows; budget-smoke fence gained the leaf as the fourth authorized recordBudgetBlock site. Failing-before proven with admission neutralized (all 3 new checks fail); host-run smoke 47/47, cross-host-review 24, budget 41, dispatch 40.

findings.desc: [codex host-B, cross_host_review B-70e9-xhr-r10] Ledger append lock can be stolen from a live writer: stale reclamation (writer.ts ~178) rmdirs the lock dir on mtime age alone; appendUsageRecord holds the lock across reading the ledger tail and appending, so a large ledger, slow filesystem, GC pause, or suspended process can exceed the 30s threshold while STILL inside the critical section - a second writer steals the live lock and appends from the same predecessor, reintroducing exactly the F-012 hash-chain corruption. Fix direction: ownership-aware reclaim - write holder pid + unique token into the lock; reclaim only when the holder process is dead (pid liveness like the slot registry) or heartbeat genuinely stale; release only if the token still matches; alternatively never steal and skip on timeout.
